faq.q: Does this actually send the message for me?
faq.a: No. It only builds click-to-chat links (wa.me and api.whatsapp.com) and QR codes. Opening one launches WhatsApp with your message pre-typed into the chat, but you still press send yourself — nothing is ever sent automatically. That's true of the bulk tab too, which only generates personalised links.

faq.q: How does it clean up the phone number I type?
faq.a: You pick a country code (26 options, India +91 default) and enter the national number; the tool strips spaces, dashes, brackets and the plus sign, removes leading zeros, and even removes a duplicated country code if you paste the full international number. It then flags numbers that look too short (under 6 digits) or too long (over 14) and shows the final +code number.

faq.q: Can I generate links for many numbers at once?
faq.a: Yes, in the Bulk tab. Paste one number per line, optionally adding a name after a comma, and write a message using {name} as a placeholder to personalise each one. It produces a table of open links plus Copy All and Download CSV. A notice warns that sending mass unsolicited messages breaks WhatsApp's Terms and can get your number banned.

faq.q: What else does it offer besides single links?
faq.a: Ready-made templates for Indian use cases (business enquiry, order/delivery, appointment and payment reminders, festival greeting, support reply, job and tuition enquiries) with fill-in fields; a formatting helper showing WhatsApp's *bold*, _italic_, ~strike~, and ```mono``` syntax with live preview; a downloadable QR code (UTF-8-aware so Hindi and emoji scan correctly); and up to 15 saved contacts stored locally under waHistory.
